Added in [1.0.0](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material#1.0.0)

```
@Composable
fun TriStateCheckbox(
 state: ToggleableState,
 onClick: (() -> Unit)?,
 modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
 enabled: Boolean = true,
 interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
 colors: CheckboxColors = CheckboxDefaults.colors()
): Unit
```

[Material Design checkbox](https://material.io/components/checkboxes)

Checkboxes can have a parent-child relationship with other checkboxes. When the parent checkbox is checked, all child checkboxes are checked. If a parent checkbox is unchecked, all child checkboxes are unchecked. If some, but not all, child checkboxes are checked, the parent checkbox becomes an indeterminate checkbox.

![Checkboxes image](https://developer.android.com/images/reference/androidx/compose/material/checkboxes.png)

```
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.Spacer
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
importandroidx.compose.material.Checkbox
importandroidx.compose.material.CheckboxDefaults
importandroidx.compose.material.MaterialTheme
importandroidx.compose.material.TriStateCheckbox
importandroidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
importandroidx.compose.runtime.remember
importandroidx.compose.ui.Modifier
importandroidx.compose.ui.state.ToggleableState
importandroidx.compose.ui.unit.dp

Column{
// define dependent checkboxes states
val(state,onStateChange)=remember{mutableStateOf(true)}
val(state2,onStateChange2)=remember{mutableStateOf(true)}

// TriStateCheckbox state reflects state of dependent checkboxes
valparentState=
remember(state,state2){
if(state && state2)ToggleableState.On
elseif(!state && !state2)ToggleableState.OffelseToggleableState.Indeterminate
}
// click on TriStateCheckbox can set state for dependent checkboxes
valonParentClick={
vals=parentState!=ToggleableState.On
onStateChange(s)
onStateChange2(s)
}

TriStateCheckbox(
state=parentState,
onClick=onParentClick,
colors=CheckboxDefaults.colors(checkedColor=MaterialTheme.colors.primary)
)
Spacer(Modifier.size(25.dp))
Column(Modifier.padding(10.dp,0.dp,0.dp,0.dp)){
Checkbox(state,onStateChange)
Spacer(Modifier.size(25.dp))
Checkbox(state2,onStateChange2)
}
}
```

| Parameters |
| --- |
| `state: ToggleableState` | whether TriStateCheckbox is checked, unchecked or in indeterminate state |
| `onClick: (() -> Unit)?` | callback to be invoked when checkbox is being clicked, therefore the change of ToggleableState state is requested. If null, then this is passive and relies entirely on a higher-level component to control the state. |
| `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` | Modifier to be applied to the layout of the checkbox |
| `enabled: Boolean = true` | whether the component is enabled or grayed out |
| `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null` | an optional hoisted `MutableInteractionSource` for observing and emitting `Interaction` s for this checkbox. You can use this to change the checkbox's appearance or preview the checkbox in different states. Note that if `null` is provided, interactions will still happen internally. |
| `colors: CheckboxColors = CheckboxDefaults.colors()` | `CheckboxColors` that will be used to determine the color of the checkmark / box / border in different states. See `CheckboxDefaults.colors`. |

| See also |
| --- |
| `Checkbox` | if you want a simple component that represents Boolean state |

### contentColorFor

[View Source](https://cs.android.com/search?q=file:androidx/compose/material/Colors.kt+function:contentColorFor)

```
@Composable
fun contentColorFor(backgroundColor: Color): Color
```

The Material color system contains pairs of colors that are typically used for the background and content color inside a component. For example, a `Button` typically uses `primary` for its background, and `onPrimary` for the color of its content (usually text or iconography).

This function tries to match the provided `backgroundColor` to a 'background' color in this `Colors`, and then will return the corresponding color used for content. For example, when `backgroundColor` is `Colors.primary`, this will return `Colors.onPrimary`.

If `backgroundColor` does not match a background color in the theme, this will return the current value of `LocalContentColor` as a best-effort color.

| Returns |
| --- |
| `Color` | the matching content color for `backgroundColor`. If `backgroundColor` is not present in the theme's `Colors`, then returns the current value of `LocalContentColor`. |

| See also |
| --- |
| `contentColorFor` | |

### ripple
Cmn

Artifact: [androidx.compose.material:material](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material)

[View Source](https://cs.android.com/search?q=file:androidx/compose/material/Ripple.kt+function:ripple)

```
fun ripple(
 bounded: Boolean = true,
 radius: Dp = Dp.Unspecified,
 color: Color = Color.Unspecified
): IndicationNodeFactory
```

Creates a Ripple using the provided values and values inferred from the theme.

A Ripple is a Material implementation of `Indication` that expresses different `Interaction` s by drawing ripple animations and state layers.

A Ripple responds to `PressInteraction.Press` by starting a new animation, and responds to other `Interaction` s by showing a fixed state layer with varying alpha values depending on the `Interaction`.

`MaterialTheme` provides Ripples using `androidx.compose.foundation.LocalIndication`, so a Ripple will be used as the default `Indication` inside components such as `androidx.compose.foundation.clickable` and `androidx.compose.foundation.indication`, in addition to Material provided components that use a Ripple as well.

You can also explicitly create a Ripple and provide it to custom components in order to change the parameters from the default, such as to create an unbounded ripple with a fixed size.

To create a Ripple with a manually defined color that can change over time, see the other `ripple` overload with a `ColorProducer` parameter. This will avoid unnecessary recompositions when changing the color, and preserve existing ripple state when the color changes.

| Parameters |
| --- |
| `bounded: Boolean = true` | If true, ripples are clipped by the bounds of the target layout. Unbounded ripples always animate from the target layout center, bounded ripples animate from the touch position. |
| `radius: Dp = Dp.Unspecified` | the radius for the ripple. If `Dp.Unspecified` is provided then the size will be calculated based on the target layout size. |
| `color: Color = Color.Unspecified` | the color of the ripple. This color is usually the same color used by the text or iconography in the component. This color will then have `RippleDefaults.rippleAlpha` applied to calculate the final color used to draw the ripple. If `Color.Unspecified` is provided the color used will be `RippleDefaults.rippleColor` instead. |

@Composable
fun RowScope.BottomNavigationItem(
 selected: Boolean,
 onClick: () -> Unit,
 icon: @Composable () -> Unit,
 modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
 enabled: Boolean = true,

```

[Material Design bottom navigation](https://material.io/components/bottom-navigation)

The recommended configuration for a BottomNavigationItem depends on how many items there are inside a `BottomNavigation`:

- Three destinations: Display icons and text labels for all destinations.

- Four destinations: Active destinations display an icon and text label. Inactive destinations display icons, and text labels are recommended.

- Five destinations: Active destinations display an icon and text label. Inactive destinations use icons, and use text labels if space permits.


A BottomNavigationItem always shows text labels (if it exists) when selected. Showing text labels if not selected is controlled by `alwaysShowLabel`.

| Parameters |
| --- |
| `selected: Boolean` | whether this item is selected |
| `onClick: () -> Unit` | the callback to be invoked when this item is selected |
| `icon: @Composable () -> Unit` | icon for this item, typically this will be an `Icon` |
| `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` | optional `Modifier` for this item |
| `enabled: Boolean = true` | controls the enabled state of this item. When `false`, this item will not be clickable and will appear disabled to accessibility services. |
| `label: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null` | optional text label for this item |
| `alwaysShowLabel: Boolean = true` | whether to always show the label for this item. If false, the label will only be shown when this item is selected. |
| `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null` | an optional hoisted `MutableInteractionSource` for observing and emitting `Interaction` s for this item. You can use this to change the item's appearance or preview the item in different states. Note that if `null` is provided, interactions will still happen internally. |
| `selectedContentColor: Color = LocalContentColor.current` | the color of the text label and icon when this item is selected, and the color of the ripple. |
| `unselectedContentColor: Color = selectedContentColor.copy(alpha = ContentAlpha.medium)` | the color of the text label and icon when this item is not selected |

### contentColorFor

```
fun Colors.contentColorFor(backgroundColor: Color): Color
```

The Material color system contains pairs of colors that are typically used for the background and content color inside a component. For example, a `Button` typically uses `primary` for its background, and `onPrimary` for the color of its content (usually text or iconography).

This function tries to match the provided `backgroundColor` to a 'background' color in this `Colors`, and then will return the corresponding color used for content. For example, when `backgroundColor` is `Colors.primary`, this will return `Colors.onPrimary`.

If `backgroundColor` does not match a background color in the theme, this will return `Color.Unspecified`.

| Returns |
| --- |
| `Color` | the matching content color for `backgroundColor`. If `backgroundColor` is not present in the theme's `Colors`, then returns `Color.Unspecified`. |

### minimumInteractiveComponentSize
Cmn

Artifact: [androidx.compose.material:material](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material)

[View Source](https://cs.android.com/search?q=file:androidx/compose/material/InteractiveComponentSize.kt+function:minimumInteractiveComponentSize)

Added in [1.4.0](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material#1.4.0)

```
fun Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize(): Modifier
```

Reserves at least 48.dp in size to disambiguate touch interactions if the element would measure smaller.

https://m2.material.io/design/usability/accessibility.html#layout-and-typography

This uses the Material recommended minimum size of 48.dp x 48.dp, which may not the same as the system enforced minimum size. The minimum clickable / touch target size (48.dp by default) is controlled by the system via `ViewConfiguration` and automatically expanded at the touch input layer.

This modifier is not needed for touch target expansion to happen. It only affects layout, to make sure there is adequate space for touch target expansion.

Because layout constraints are affected by modifier order, for this modifier to take effect, it must come before any size modifiers on the element that might limit its constraints.

### swipeable
Cmn

Artifact: [androidx.compose.material:material](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material)

[View Source](https://cs.android.com/search?q=file:androidx/compose/material/Swipeable.kt+function:swipeable)

```
@ExperimentalMaterialApi
fun Modifier.swipeable(
 state: SwipeableState,
 anchors: Map,
 orientation: Orientation,
 enabled: Boolean = true,
 reverseDirection: Boolean = false,
 interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
 thresholds: (from, to) -> ThresholdConfig = { _, _ -> FixedThreshold(56.dp) },
 resistance: ResistanceConfig? = resistanceConfig(anchors.keys),
 velocityThreshold: Dp = VelocityThreshold
): Modifier
```

Enable swipe gestures between a set of predefined states.

To use this, you must provide a map of anchors (in pixels) to states (of type `T`). Note that this map cannot be empty and cannot have two anchors mapped to the same state.

When a swipe is detected, the offset of the `SwipeableState` will be updated with the swipe delta. You should use this offset to move your content accordingly (see `Modifier.offsetPx`). When the swipe ends, the offset will be animated to one of the anchors and when that anchor is reached, the value of the `SwipeableState` will also be updated to the state corresponding to the new anchor. The target anchor is calculated based on the provided positional `thresholds`.

Swiping is constrained between the minimum and maximum anchors. If the user attempts to swipe past these bounds, a resistance effect will be applied by default. The amount of resistance at each edge is specified by the `resistance` config. To disable all resistance, set it to `null`.

For an example of a `swipeable` with three states, see:

```
importandroidx.compose.foundation.background
importandroidx.compose.foundation.gestures.Orientation
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.offset
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.width
importandroidx.compose.material.FractionalThreshold
importandroidx.compose.material.Text
importandroidx.compose.material.rememberSwipeableState
importandroidx.compose.material.swipeable
importandroidx.compose.ui.Alignment
importandroidx.compose.ui.Modifier
importandroidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
importandroidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalDensity
importandroidx.compose.ui.unit.IntOffset
importandroidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
importandroidx.compose.ui.unit.sp

// Draw a slider-like composable consisting of a red square moving along a
// black background, with three states: "A" (min), "B" (middle), and "C" (max).
valwidth=350.dp
valsquareSize=50.dp

valswipeableState=rememberSwipeableState("A")
valsizePx=with(LocalDensity.current){(width-squareSize).toPx()}
valanchors=mapOf(0fto"A",sizePx/2to"B",sizePxto"C")

Box(
modifier=
Modifier.width(width)
.swipeable(
state=swipeableState,
anchors=anchors,
thresholds={_,_->FractionalThreshold(0.5f)},
orientation=Orientation.Horizontal
)
.background(Color.Black)
){
Box(
Modifier.offset{IntOffset(swipeableState.offset.value.roundToInt(),0)}
.size(squareSize)
.background(Color.Red),
contentAlignment=Alignment.Center
){
Text(swipeableState.currentValue,color=Color.White,fontSize=24.sp)
}
}
```


### swipeable

| Parameters |
| --- |
| ` ` | The type of the state. |
| `state: SwipeableState ` | The state of the `swipeable`. |
| `anchors: Map ` | Pairs of anchors and states, used to map anchors to states and vice versa. |
| `orientation: Orientation` | The orientation in which the `swipeable` can be swiped. |
| `enabled: Boolean = true` | Whether this `swipeable` is enabled and should react to the user's input. |
| `reverseDirection: Boolean = false` | Whether to reverse the direction of the swipe, so a top to bottom swipe will behave like bottom to top, and a left to right swipe will behave like right to left. |
| `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null` | Optional `MutableInteractionSource` that will passed on to the internal `Modifier.draggable`. |
| `thresholds: (from, to) -> ThresholdConfig = { _, _ -> FixedThreshold(56.dp) }` | Specifies where the thresholds between the states are. The thresholds will be used to determine which state to animate to when swiping stops. This is represented as a lambda that takes two states and returns the threshold between them in the form of a `ThresholdConfig`. Note that the order of the states corresponds to the swipe direction. |
| `resistance: ResistanceConfig? = resistanceConfig(anchors.keys)` | Controls how much resistance will be applied when swiping past the bounds. |
| `velocityThreshold: Dp = VelocityThreshold` | The threshold (in dp per second) that the end velocity has to exceed in order to animate to the next state, even if the positional `thresholds` have not been reached. |

CompositionLocal containing the preferred content alpha for a given position in the hierarchy. This alpha is used for text and iconography ( `Text` and `Icon`) to emphasize / de-emphasize different parts of a component. See the Material guide on [Text Legibility](https://material.io/design/color/text-legibility.html) for more information on alpha levels used by text and iconography.

See `ContentAlpha` for the default levels used by most Material components.

`MaterialTheme` sets this to `ContentAlpha.high` by default, as this is the default alpha for body text.

```
importandroidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
importandroidx.compose.material.ContentAlpha
importandroidx.compose.material.LocalContentAlpha
importandroidx.compose.material.Text
importandroidx.compose.runtime.CompositionLocalProvider

// Note the alpha values listed below are the values for light theme. The values are slightly
// different in dark theme to provide proper contrast against the background.
Column{
Text(
"No content alpha applied - uses the default content alpha set by MaterialTheme - "+
"87% alpha"
)
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentAlphaprovides1.00f){
Text("1.00f alpha applied - 100% alpha")
}
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentAlphaprovidesContentAlpha.high){
Text("High content alpha applied - 87% alpha")
}
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentAlphaprovidesContentAlpha.medium){
Text("Medium content alpha applied - 60% alpha")
}
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalContentAlphaprovidesContentAlpha.disabled){
Text("Disabled content alpha applied - 38% alpha")
}
}
```

# https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/androidx/compose/material3/package-summary
# androidx.compose.material3
Common/AllAndroid/JVM

Build Jetpack Compose UIs with [Material Design 3](https://m3.material.io), the next evolution of Material Design. Material 3 includes updated theming and components and Material You personalization features like dynamic color, and is designed to be cohesive with the new Android 12 visual style and system UI.

![Material You image](https://developer.android.com/images/reference/androidx/compose/material3/material-you.png)

In this page, you'll find documentation for types, properties, and functions available in the `androidx.compose.material3` package.

For more information, check out [Material Design 3 in Compose](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/compose/designsystems/material3).

### Icon
Cmn

Artifact: [androidx.compose.material3:material3](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material3)

[View Source](https://cs.android.com/search?q=file:androidx/compose/material3/Icon.kt+function:Icon)

Added in [1.3.0](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material3#1.3.0)

```
@Composable
@ExperimentalMaterial3Api
fun Icon(
 painter: Painter,
 tint: ColorProducer?,
 contentDescription: String?,
 modifier: Modifier = Modifier
): Unit
```

A Material Design icon component that draws `painter` using `tint`. If `painter` has no intrinsic size, this component will use the recommended default size. Icon is an opinionated component designed to be used with single-color icons so that they can be tinted correctly for the component they are placed in. For multicolored icons and icons that should not be tinted, use null for `tint`. For generic images that should not be tinted, and do not follow the recommended icon size, use the generic `androidx.compose.foundation.Image` instead. For a clickable icon, see `IconButton`.

To learn more about icons, see [Material Design icons](https://m3.material.io/styles/icons/overview)

| Parameters |
| --- |
| `painter: Painter` | `Painter` to draw inside this icon |
| `tint: ColorProducer?` | tint to be applied to `painter`. If null, then no tint is applied. |
| `contentDescription: String?` | text used by accessibility services to describe what this icon represents. This should always be provided unless this icon is used for decorative purposes, and does not represent a meaningful action that a user can take. This text should be localized, such as by using androidx.compose.ui.res.stringResource or similar |
| `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` | the `Modifier` to be applied to this icon |

### IconToggleButton
Cmn

Artifact: [androidx.compose.material3:material3](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material3)

[View Source](https://cs.android.com/search?q=file:androidx/compose/material3/IconButton.kt+function:IconToggleButton)

Added in [1.4.0-alpha14](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material3#1.4.0-alpha14)

```
@Composable
fun IconToggleButton(
 checked: Boolean,
 onCheckedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit,
 modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
 enabled: Boolean = true,
 colors: IconToggleButtonColors = IconButtonDefaults.iconToggleButtonColors(),
 interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null,
 shape: Shape = IconButtonDefaults.standardShape,
 content: @Composable () -> Unit
): Unit
```

[Material Design standard icon toggle button](https://m3.material.io/components/icon-button/overview)

Icon buttons help people take supplementary actions with a single tap. They’re used when a compact button is required, such as in a toolbar or image list.

![Standard icon toggle button image](https://developer.android.com/images/reference/androidx/compose/material3/standard-icon-toggle-button.png)

`content` should typically be an `Icon` (see `androidx.compose.material.icons.Icons`). If using a custom icon, note that the typical size for the internal icon is 24 x 24 dp. This icon button has an overall minimum touch target size of 48 x 48dp, to meet accessibility guidelines.

```
importandroidx.compose.material.icons.Icons
importandroidx.compose.material.icons.filled.Lock
importandroidx.compose.material.icons.outlined.Lock
importandroidx.compose.material3.Icon
importandroidx.compose.material3.IconToggleButton
importandroidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
importandroidx.compose.runtime.remember

varcheckedbyremember{mutableStateOf(false)}
IconToggleButton(checked=checked,onCheckedChange={checked=it}){
if(checked){
Icon(Icons.Filled.Lock,contentDescription="Localized description")
}else{
Icon(Icons.Outlined.Lock,contentDescription="Localized description")
}
}
```

| Parameters |
| --- |
| `checked: Boolean` | whether this icon button is toggled on or off |
| `onCheckedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit` | called when this icon button is clicked |
| `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` | the `Modifier` to be applied to this icon button |
| `enabled: Boolean = true` | controls the enabled state of this icon button. When `false`, this component will not respond to user input, and it will appear visually disabled and disabled to accessibility services. |
| `colors: IconToggleButtonColors = IconButtonDefaults.iconToggleButtonColors()` | `IconToggleButtonColors` that will be used to resolve the colors used for this icon button in different states. See `IconButtonDefaults.iconToggleButtonVibrantColors` and `IconButtonDefaults.iconToggleButtonColors`. |
| `interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null` | an optional hoisted `MutableInteractionSource` for observing and emitting `Interaction` s for this icon button. You can use this to change the icon button's appearance or preview the icon button in different states. Note that if `null` is provided, interactions will still happen internally. |
| `shape: Shape = IconButtonDefaults.standardShape` | the `Shape` of this icon button. |
| `content: @Composable () -> Unit` | the content of this icon button, typically an `Icon` |

Ejecuta la aplicación en un dispositivo o emulador\n\n## Estructura del Proyecto\n\n### Domain Layer (Capa de Dominio)\n\n**Modelos:**\n- `Song` - Entidad que representa una canción\n- `PlayerState` - Estado del reproductor\n- `PlaybackState` - Estados de reproducción\n\n**Use Cases:**\n- `GetSongsUseCase` - Obtener lista de canciones\n- `PlaySongUseCase` - Reproducir una canción\n- `GetPlayerStateUseCase` - Obtener estado del reproductor\n- `ControlPlaybackUseCase` - Controlar reproducción\n\n### Data Layer (Capa de Datos)\n\n**Repositorios:**\n- `MusicRepositoryImpl` - Implementación del repositorio de música\n- `PlayerRepositoryImpl` - Implementación del repositorio del reproductor\n\n**Services:**\n- `MusicService` - MediaSessionService para reproducción en background\n\n### Presentation Layer (Capa de Presentación)\n\n**ViewModels:**\n- `MusicPlayerViewModel` - Maneja la lógica de la UI y el estado\n\n**UI:**\n- `MusicPlayerScreen` - Pantalla principal del reproductor\n- `SongItem` - Componente de item de canción\n- `MiniPlayer` - Componente de controles del reproductor\n\n## Características de UI\n\n- **Material Design 3** con colores dinámicos\n- **Animaciones suaves** en transiciones\n- **Diseño responsive** que se adapta a diferentes tamaños de pantalla\n- **Dark/Light Theme** soporte automático\n- **Iconos Material** para una experiencia consistente\n\n## Funcionalidades del Reproductor\n\n- ▶️ Play/Pause\n- ⏭️ Skip to Next\n- ⏮️ Skip to Previous\n- ️ Seek (navegar en la canción)\n- Lista de reproducción\n- ️ Artwork de álbum\n- Reproducción en background\n- Controles de notificación\n\n## Testing\n\nEl proyecto está preparado para:\n- Unit Tests (Domain Layer)\n- Integration Tests (Data Layer)\n- UI Tests (Presentation Layer)\n\n## Licencia\n\nEste proyecto es de código abierto y está disponible bajo la licencia MIT.\n\n## ‍ Autor\n\nTu Nombre - [@tuusuario](https://github.com/tuusuario)\n\n## Contribuciones\n\nLas contribuciones son bienvenidas! +# Music Player with Media3 & MediaSession - Clean Architecture
 
+Un reproductor de música moderno para Android construido con **Jetpack Compose**, **Media3**, *
+*MediaSession** y siguiendo los principios de **Clean Architecture**.
+
+![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-3DDC84?style=for-the-badge&logo=android&logoColor=white)
+![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-0095D5?&style=for-the-badge&logo=kotlin&logoColor=white)
+![Jetpack Compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jetpack%20Compose-4285F4?style=for-the-badge&logo=jetpackcompose&logoColor=white)
+
+## Características
+
+- ✅ Reproducción de música con Media3 ExoPlayer
+- ✅ Control de reproducción con MediaSession
+- ✅ UI moderna con Jetpack Compose y Material Design 3
+- ✅ Reproducción en segundo plano
+- ✅ Controles de reproducción (Play, Pause, Next, Previous, Seek)
+- ✅ Lista de canciones con diseño atractivo
+- ✅ Visualización de artwork de álbumes
+- ✅ Arquitectura limpia y escalable
+
+## ️ Arquitectura
+
+El proyecto sigue los principios de **Clean Architecture** con tres capas principales:
+
+### Capas
+
+```
+app/
+├── data/ # Capa de Datos
+│ ├── repository/ # Implementaciones de repositorios
+│ └── service/ # MediaSessionService
+├── domain/ # Capa de Dominio
+│ ├── model/ # Entidades del dominio
+│ ├── repository/ # Interfaces de repositorios
+│ └── usecase/ # Casos de uso
+└── presentation/ # Capa de Presentación
+ ├── ui/ # Componentes de UI (Compose)
+ └── viewmodel/ # ViewModels
+```
+
+### Flujo de Datos
+
+```
+UI (Compose) → ViewModel → Use Cases → Repository → Data Source
+ ↓
+ State/Events
+```
+
+## ️ Tecnologías Utilizadas
+
+- **Kotlin** - Lenguaje de programación
+- **Jetpack Compose** - UI moderna y declarativa
+- **Material Design 3** - Sistema de diseño
+- **Media3** - Framework de reproducción multimedia
+- **MediaSession** - Control de sesión de medios
+- **Hilt** - Inyección de dependencias
+- **Coroutines & Flow** - Programación asíncrona
+- **Coil** - Carga de imágenes
+- **Clean Architecture** - Patrón arquitectónico
+

+
+- Android Studio Hedgehog | 2023.1.1 o superior
+- Minimum SDK: 24 (Android 7.0)
+- Target SDK: 35 (Android 15)
+- Kotlin 2.0.21
+- Gradle 8.10.1

+

+
+4. Ejecuta la aplicación en un dispositivo o emulador
+
+## Estructura del Proyecto
+
+### Domain Layer (Capa de Dominio)
+
+**Modelos:**
+
+- `Song` - Entidad que representa una canción

+
+**Use Cases:**

+- `ControlPlaybackUseCase` - Controlar reproducción
+
+### Data Layer (Capa de Datos)
+
+**Repositorios:**
+
+- `MusicRepositoryImpl` - Implementación del repositorio de música
+- `PlayerRepositoryImpl` - Implementación del repositorio del reproductor
+
+**Services:**
+
+- `MusicService` - MediaSessionService para reproducción en background
+
+### Presentation Layer (Capa de Presentación)
+
+**ViewModels:**
+

+
+**UI:**
+

+- `MiniPlayer` - Componente de controles del reproductor

## Reproductor de Música - Completado

### ✅ Lo que hemos creado:

#### **1. Arquitectura Clean (Domain Layer)**
- ✅ `Song` - Modelo de dominio para canciones
- ✅ `PlayerState` - Estado del reproductor
- ✅ `MusicRepository` interface
- ✅ `PlayerRepository` interface
- ✅ Use Cases: `GetSongsUseCase`, `PlaySongUseCase`, `GetPlayerStateUseCase`, `ControlPlaybackUseCase`

#### **2. Data Layer**
- ✅ `MusicRepositoryImpl` - Con canciones de ejemplo
- ✅ `PlayerRepositoryImpl` - Integración con Media3
- ✅ `MusicService` - MediaSessionService para reproducción en background

#### **3. Presentation Layer**
- ✅ `MusicPlayerViewModel` - Maneja el estado y la lógica
- ✅ `MusicPlayerScreen` - UI principal con Compose
- ✅ `SongItem` - Componente de lista de canciones
- ✅ `MiniPlayer` - Controles de reproducción

#### **4. Dependency Injection**
- ✅ `AppModule` - Módulo Hilt con todas las dependencias
- ✅ `MusicPlayerApp` - Application class con Hilt

#### **5. Configuración**
- ✅ `MainActivity` - Con integración de Hilt y ViewModel
- ✅ `AndroidManifest.xml` - Con permisos y servicio configurado
- ✅ `build.gradle.kts` - Con todas las dependencias (Media3, Hilt, Coil)
- ✅ `README.md` - Documentación completa

### Características del Reproductor:

1. **Lista de Canciones**: Muestra 5 canciones de ejemplo con artwork
2. **Reproducción**: Play, Pause, Next, Previous
3. **Seek Bar**: Navegar dentro de la canción
4. **UI Moderna**: Material Design 3 con Jetpack Compose
5. **Background Playback**: Reproducción en segundo plano con MediaSession
6. **Estado Reactivo**: Usando Flow para actualizaciones en tiempo real

### Para ejecutar el proyecto:

1. Abre el proyecto en Android Studio
2. Sincroniza Gradle
3. Ejecuta en un emulador o dispositivo físico (API 24+)
4. Las canciones de ejemplo se cargarán automáticamente

### Funcionalidades:

- Tap en una canción para reproducirla
- Botón Play/Pause para controlar reproducción
- Flechas para ir a la siguiente/anterior canción
- Slider para navegar en la canción
- Indicador visual de la canción actual
- Timer de duración de la canción

### ️ Ventajas de Clean Architecture:

- **Testeable**: Cada capa se puede testear independientemente
- **Mantenible**: Código organizado y fácil de mantener
- **Escalable**: Fácil agregar nuevas features
- **Desacoplado**: Las capas no dependen de implementaciones concretas
- **Reutilizable**: Los Use Cases pueden ser reutilizados

- Favoritos

+package com.example.mediasessionplayer.data.service
+
+import android.app.PendingIntent
+import android.content.Intent
+import androidx.media3.common.AudioAttributes
+import androidx.media3.common.C
+import androidx.media3.common.MediaItem
+import androidx.media3.common.Player
+import androidx.media3.exoplayer.ExoPlayer
+import androidx.media3.session.MediaSession
+import androidx.media3.session.MediaSessionService
+import dagger.hilt.android.AndroidEntryPoint
+import javax.inject.Inject
+
+@AndroidEntryPoint
+class MusicService : MediaSessionService() {
+
+ @Inject
+ lateinit var player: ExoPlayer
+
+ private var mediaSession: MediaSession? = null
+
+ override fun onCreate() {
+ super.onCreate()
+
+ val sessionActivityPendingIntent =
+ packageManager?.getLaunchIntentForPackage(packageName)?.let { sessionIntent ->
+ PendingIntent.getActivity(
+ this,
+ 0,
+ sessionIntent,
+ PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE or PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT
+ )
+ }
+
+ mediaSession = MediaSession.Builder(this, player)
+ .setSessionActivity(sessionActivityPendingIntent!!)
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ override fun onGetSession(controllerInfo: MediaSession.ControllerInfo): MediaSession? {
+ return mediaSession
+ }
+
+ override fun onDestroy() {
+ mediaSession?.run {
+ player.release()
+ release()
+ mediaSession = null
+ }
+ super.onDestroy()
+ }
+}
+

+package com.example.mediasessionplayer.data.repository
+
+import android.content.ComponentName
+import android.content.Context
+import androidx.media3.common.MediaItem
+import androidx.media3.common.MediaMetadata
+import androidx.media3.common.Player
+import androidx.media3.session.MediaController
+import androidx.media3.session.SessionToken
+import com.example.mediasessionplayer.data.service.MusicService
+import com.example.mediasessionplayer.domain.model.PlayerState
+import com.example.mediasessionplayer.domain.model.PlaybackState
+import com.example.mediasessionplayer.domain.model.Song
+import com.example.mediasessionplayer.domain.repository.PlayerRepository
+import com.google.common.util.concurrent.ListenableFuture
+import com.google.common.util.concurrent.MoreExecutors
+import dagger.hilt.android.qualifiers.ApplicationContext
+import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
+import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
+import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
+import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow
+import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flow
+import javax.inject.Inject
+import javax.inject.Singleton
+
+@Singleton
+class PlayerRepositoryImpl @Inject constructor(
+ @ApplicationContext private val context: Context
+) : PlayerRepository {
+
+ private var mediaController: MediaController? = null
+ private var controllerFuture: ListenableFuture<MediaController>? = null
+
+ private val _playerState = MutableStateFlow(PlayerState())
+ override val playerState: Flow<PlayerState> = _playerState.asStateFlow()
+
+ private var currentPlaylist: List<Song> = emptyList()
+
+ init {
+ initializeController()
+ }
+
+ private fun initializeController() {
+ val sessionToken = SessionToken(
+ context,
+ ComponentName(context, MusicService::class.java)
+ )
+
+ controllerFuture = MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync()
+ controllerFuture?.addListener({
+ mediaController = controllerFuture?.get()
+ setupPlayerListener()
+ }, MoreExecutors.directExecutor())
+ }
+
+ private fun setupPlayerListener() {
+ mediaController?.addListener(object : Player.Listener {
+ override fun onIsPlayingChanged(isPlaying: Boolean) {
+ _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(isPlaying = isPlaying)
+ }
+
+ override fun onPlaybackStateChanged(playbackState: Int) {
+ val state = when (playbackState) {
+ Player.STATE_IDLE -> PlaybackState.IDLE
+ Player.STATE_BUFFERING -> PlaybackState.BUFFERING
+ Player.STATE_READY -> PlaybackState.READY
+ Player.STATE_ENDED -> PlaybackState.ENDED
+ else -> PlaybackState.IDLE
+ }
+ _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(
+ playbackState = state,
+ duration = mediaController?.duration ?: 0L
+ )
+ }
+
+ override fun onMediaItemTransition(mediaItem: MediaItem?, reason: Int) {
+ val currentIndex = mediaController?.currentMediaItemIndex ?: -1
+ if (currentIndex >= 0 && currentIndex < currentPlaylist.size) {
+ _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(
+ currentSong = currentPlaylist[currentIndex]
+ )
+ }
+ }
+ })
+ }
+
+ override fun play() {
+ mediaController?.play()
+ }
+
+ override fun pause() {
+ mediaController?.pause()
+ }
+
+ override fun seekTo(position: Long) {
+ mediaController?.seekTo(position)
+ }
+
+ override fun skipToNext() {
+ mediaController?.seekToNext()
+ }
+
+ override fun skipToPrevious() {
+ mediaController?.seekToPrevious()
+ }
+
+ override fun playSong(song: Song) {
+ val mediaItem = createMediaItem(song)
+ mediaController?.apply {
+ setMediaItem(mediaItem)
+ prepare()
+ play()
+ }
+ _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(currentSong = song)
+ }
+
+ override fun setPlaylist(songs: List<Song>, startIndex: Int) {
+ currentPlaylist = songs
+ val mediaItems = songs.map { createMediaItem(it) }
+
+ mediaController?.apply {
+ setMediaItems(mediaItems, startIndex, 0)
+ prepare()
+ play()
+ }
+
+ if (startIndex < songs.size) {
+ _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(currentSong = songs[startIndex])
+ }
+ }
+
+ private fun createMediaItem(song: Song): MediaItem {
+ val metadata = MediaMetadata.Builder()
+ .setTitle(song.title)
+ .setArtist(song.artist)
+ .setAlbumTitle(song.album)
+ .setArtworkUri(android.net.Uri.parse(song.imageUrl))
+ .build()
+
+ return MediaItem.Builder()
+ .setMediaId(song.id)
+ .setUri(song.mediaUri)
+ .setMediaMetadata(metadata)
+ .build()
+ }
+
+ override fun release() {
+ MediaController.releaseFuture(controllerFuture ?: return)
+ mediaController = null
+ }
+}
+

+ .setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true)
+ .build()
+ }

+ fun providePlayerRepository(

+package com.example.mediasessionplayer.presentation.viewmodel
+
+import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
+import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope

+import com.example.mediasessionplayer.domain.model.Song

+import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.stateIn
+import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
+import javax.inject.Inject
+
+@HiltViewModel
+class MusicPlayerViewModel @Inject constructor(
+ private val getSongsUseCase: GetSongsUseCase,
+ private val playSongUseCase: PlaySongUseCase,
+ private val controlPlaybackUseCase: ControlPlaybackUseCase,
+ getPlayerStateUseCase: GetPlayerStateUseCase
+) : ViewModel() {
+
+ private val _songs = MutableStateFlow<List<Song>>(emptyList())
+ val songs: StateFlow<List<Song>> = _songs.asStateFlow()
+
+ val playerState: StateFlow<PlayerState> = getPlayerStateUseCase()
+ .stateIn(
+ scope = viewModelScope,
+ started = SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000),
+ initialValue = PlayerState()
+ )
+
+ init {
+ loadSongs()
+ }
+
+ private fun loadSongs() {
+ viewModelScope.launch {
+ _songs.value = getSongsUseCase()
+ }
+ }
+
+ fun playSong(song: Song) {
+ playSongUseCase(song)
+ }
+
+ fun playPause() {
+ if (playerState.value.isPlaying) {
+ controlPlaybackUseCase.pause()
+ } else {
+ controlPlaybackUseCase.play()
+ }
+ }
+
+ fun seekTo(position: Long) {
+ controlPlaybackUseCase.seekTo(position)
+ }
+
+ fun skipToNext() {
+ controlPlaybackUseCase.skipToNext()
+ }
+
+ fun skipToPrevious() {
+ controlPlaybackUseCase.skipToPrevious()
+ }
+}
+

+package com.example.mediasessionplayer.presentation.ui
+
+import androidx.compose.foundation.background

+import androidx.compose.material.icons.automirrored.filled.ArrowForward
+import androidx.compose.material.icons.filled.*

+
+@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
+@Composable
+fun MusicPlayerScreen(
+ songs: List<Song>,
+ playerState: PlayerState,
+ onSongClick: (Song) -> Unit,
+ onPlayPauseClick: () -> Unit,
+ onSkipNext: () -> Unit,
+ onSkipPrevious: () -> Unit,
+ onSeek: (Long) -> Unit,
+ modifier: Modifier = Modifier
+) {
+ Column(
+ modifier = modifier
+ .fillMaxSize()
+ .background(
+ Brush.verticalGradient(
+ colors = listOf(
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary.copy(alpha = 0.2f),
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background
+ )
+ )
+ )
+ ) {
+ // App Bar
+ TopAppBar(
+ title = {
+ Text(
+ text = "Music Player",
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium,
+ fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold
+ )
+ },
+ colors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(
+ containerColor = Color.Transparent
+ )
+ )
+
+ // Song List
+ LazyColumn(
+ modifier = Modifier
+ .weight(1f)
+ .fillMaxWidth(),
+ contentPadding = PaddingValues(16.dp),
+ verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)
+ ) {
+ items(songs) { song ->
+ SongItem(
+ song = song,
+ isCurrentSong = playerState.currentSong?.id == song.id,
+ isPlaying = playerState.isPlaying && playerState.currentSong?.id == song.id,
+ onClick = { onSongClick(song) }
+ )
+ }
+ }
+
+ // Player Controls
+ if (playerState.currentSong != null) {
+ MiniPlayer(
+ playerState = playerState,
+ onPlayPauseClick = onPlayPauseClick,
+ onSkipNext = onSkipNext,
+ onSkipPrevious = onSkipPrevious,
+ onSeek = onSeek
+ )
+ }
+ }
+}
+
+@Composable
+fun SongItem(
+ song: Song,
+ isCurrentSong: Boolean,
+ isPlaying: Boolean,
+ onClick: () -> Unit,
+ modifier: Modifier = Modifier
+) {
+ Card(
+ modifier = modifier
+ .fillMaxWidth()
+ .clickable { onClick() },
+ elevation = CardDefaults.cardElevation(
+ defaultElevation = if (isCurrentSong) 8.dp else 2.dp
+ ),
+ colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(
+ containerColor = if (isCurrentSong)
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primaryContainer
+ else
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface
+ ),
+ shape = RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)
+ ) {
+ Row(
+ modifier = Modifier
+ .fillMaxWidth()
+ .padding(12.dp),
+ verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
+ ) {
+ // Album Art
+ AsyncImage(
+ model = song.imageUrl,
+ contentDescription = "Album art for ${song.title}",
+ modifier = Modifier
+ .size(60.dp)
+ .clip(RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)),
+ contentScale = ContentScale.Crop
+ )
+
+ Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(12.dp))
+
+ // Song Info
+ Column(
+ modifier = Modifier.weight(1f)
+ ) {
+ Text(
+ text = song.title,
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
+ fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold,
+ maxLines = 1,
+ overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
+ color = if (isCurrentSong)
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimaryContainer
+ else
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface
+ )
+ Text(
+ text = song.artist,
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
+ maxLines = 1,
+ overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
+ color = if (isCurrentSong)
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimaryContainer.copy(alpha = 0.7f)
+ else
+ MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
+ )
+ }
+
+ // Playing indicator
+ if (isPlaying) {
+ Icon(
+ imageVector = Icons.Filled.PlayArrow,
+ contentDescription = "Now playing",
+ tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary,
+ modifier = Modifier.size(24.dp)
+ )
+ }
+ }
+ }
+}
+
+@Composable
+fun MiniPlayer(
+ playerState: PlayerState,
+ onPlayPauseClick: () -> Unit,
+ onSkipNext: () -> Unit,
+ onSkipPrevious: () -> Unit,
+ onSeek: (Long) -> Unit,
+ modifier: Modifier = Modifier
+) {
+ val song = playerState.currentSong ?: return
+
+ Surface(
+ modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
+ color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceVariant,
+ shadowElevation = 8.dp
+ ) {
+ Column(
+ modifier = Modifier
+ .fillMaxWidth()
+ .padding(16.dp)
+ ) {
+ // Current Song Info
+ Row(
+ modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
+ verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
+ ) {
+ AsyncImage(
+ model = song.imageUrl,
+ contentDescription = "Album art",
+ modifier = Modifier
+ .size(56.dp)
+ .clip(RoundedCornerShape(8.dp)),
+ contentScale = ContentScale.Crop
+ )
+
+ Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(12.dp))
+
+ Column(modifier = Modifier.weight(1f)) {
+ Text(
+ text = song.title,
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
+ fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold,
+ maxLines = 1,
+ overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis
+ )
+ Text(
+ text = song.artist,
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
+ color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
+ maxLines = 1,
+ overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis
+ )
+ }
+ }
+
+ Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))
+
+ // Progress Bar
+ var sliderPosition by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
+
+ LaunchedEffect(playerState.currentPosition) {
+ sliderPosition = playerState.currentPosition.toFloat()
+ }
+
+ Slider(
+ value = sliderPosition,
+ onValueChange = { sliderPosition = it },
+ onValueChangeFinished = { onSeek(sliderPosition.toLong()) },
+ valueRange = 0f..playerState.duration.toFloat().coerceAtLeast(1f),
+ modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
+ )
+
+ Row(
+ modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
+ horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween
+ ) {
+ Text(
+ text = formatDuration(sliderPosition.toLong()),
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
+ color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
+ )
+ Text(
+ text = formatDuration(playerState.duration),
+ style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
+ color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
+ )
+ }
+
+ Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(8.dp))
+
+ // Playback Controls
+ Row(
+ modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
+ horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceEvenly,
+ verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
+ ) {
+ IconButton(
+ onClick = onSkipPrevious,
+ modifier = Modifier.size(56.dp)
+ ) {
+ Icon(
+ imageVector = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack,
+ contentDescription = "Previous",
+ modifier = Modifier.size(32.dp)
+ )
+ }
+
+ FilledIconButton(
+ onClick = onPlayPauseClick,
+ modifier = Modifier.size(64.dp),
+ shape = CircleShape
+ ) {
+ Icon(
+ imageVector = if (playerState.isPlaying) Icons.Filled.Close else Icons.Filled.PlayArrow,
+ contentDescription = if (playerState.isPlaying) "Pause" else "Play",
+ modifier = Modifier.size(36.dp)
+ )
+ }
+
+ IconButton(
+ onClick = onSkipNext,
+ modifier = Modifier.size(56.dp)
+ ) {
+ Icon(
+ imageVector = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowForward,
+ contentDescription = "Next",
+ modifier = Modifier.size(32.dp)
+ )
+ }
+ }
+ }
+ }
+}
+
+private fun formatDuration(millis: Long): String {
+ val totalSeconds = millis / 1000
+ val minutes = totalSeconds / 60
+ val seconds = totalSeconds % 60
+ return String.format("%d:%02d", minutes, seconds)
+}
+

+# Music Player with Media3 & MediaSession - Clean Architecture
+
+Un reproductor de música moderno para Android construido con **Jetpack Compose**, **Media3**, *
+*MediaSession** y siguiendo los principios de **Clean Architecture**.
+
+![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-3DDC84?style=for-the-badge&logo=android&logoColor=white)
+![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-0095D5?&style=for-the-badge&logo=kotlin&logoColor=white)
+![Jetpack Compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jetpack%20Compose-4285F4?style=for-the-badge&logo=jetpackcompose&logoColor=white)
+
+## Características
+
+- ✅ Reproducción de música con Media3 ExoPlayer
+- ✅ Control de reproducción con MediaSession
+- ✅ UI moderna con Jetpack Compose y Material Design 3
+- ✅ Reproducción en segundo plano
+- ✅ Controles de reproducción (Play, Pause, Next, Previous, Seek)
+- ✅ Lista de canciones con diseño atractivo
+- ✅ Visualización de artwork de álbumes
+- ✅ Arquitectura limpia y escalable
+
+## ️ Arquitectura
+
+El proyecto sigue los principios de **Clean Architecture** con tres capas principales:
+
+### Capas
+
+```
+app/
+├── data/ # Capa de Datos
+│ ├── repository/ # Implementaciones de repositorios
+│ └── service/ # MediaSessionService
+├── domain/ # Capa de Dominio
+│ ├── model/ # Entidades del dominio
+│ ├── repository/ # Interfaces de repositorios
+│ └── usecase/ # Casos de uso
+└── presentation/ # Capa de Presentación
+ ├── ui/ # Componentes de UI (Compose)
+ └── viewmodel/ # ViewModels
+```
+
+### Flujo de Datos
+
+```
+UI (Compose) → ViewModel → Use Cases → Repository → Data Source
+ ↓
+ State/Events
+```
+
+## ️ Tecnologías Utilizadas
+
+- **Kotlin** - Lenguaje de programación
+- **Jetpack Compose** - UI moderna y declarativa
+- **Material Design 3** - Sistema de diseño
+- **Media3** - Framework de reproducción multimedia
+- **MediaSession** - Control de sesión de medios
+- **Hilt** - Inyección de dependencias
+- **Coroutines & Flow** - Programación asíncrona
+- **Coil** - Carga de imágenes
+- **Clean Architecture** - Patrón arquitectónico
+
+## Requisitos
+
+- Android Studio Hedgehog | 2023.1.1 o superior
+- Minimum SDK: 24 (Android 7.0)
+- Target SDK: 35 (Android 15)
+- Kotlin 2.0.21
+- Gradle 8.10.1
+
+## Instalación
+
+1. Clona el repositorio:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/tuusuario/mediasessionplayer.git
+```
+
+2. Abre el proyecto en Android Studio
+
+3. Sincroniza el proyecto con Gradle
+
+4. Ejecuta la aplicación en un dispositivo o emulador
+
+## Estructura del Proyecto
+
+### Domain Layer (Capa de Dominio)
+
+**Modelos:**
+
+- `Song` - Entidad que representa una canción
+- `PlayerState` - Estado del reproductor
+- `PlaybackState` - Estados de reproducción
+
+**Use Cases:**
+
+- `GetSongsUseCase` - Obtener lista de canciones
+- `PlaySongUseCase` - Reproducir una canción
+- `GetPlayerStateUseCase` - Obtener estado del reproductor
+- `ControlPlaybackUseCase` - Controlar reproducción
+
+### Data Layer (Capa de Datos)
+
+**Repositorios:**
+
+- `MusicRepositoryImpl` - Implementación del repositorio de música
+- `PlayerRepositoryImpl` - Implementación del repositorio del reproductor
+
+**Services:**
+
+- `MusicService` - MediaSessionService para reproducción en background
+
+### Presentation Layer (Capa de Presentación)
+
+**ViewModels:**
+
+- `MusicPlayerViewModel` - Maneja la lógica de la UI y el estado
+
+**UI:**
+
+- `MusicPlayerScreen` - Pantalla principal del reproductor
+- `SongItem` - Componente de item de canción
+- `MiniPlayer` - Componente de controles del reproductor
+
+## Características de UI
+
+- **Material Design 3** con colores dinámicos
+- **Animaciones suaves** en transiciones
+- **Diseño responsive** que se adapta a diferentes tamaños de pantalla
+- **Dark/Light Theme** soporte automático
+- **Iconos Material** para una experiencia consistente
+
+## Funcionalidades del Reproductor
+
+- ▶️ Play/Pause
+- ⏭️ Skip to Next
+- ⏮️ Skip to Previous
+- ️ Seek (navegar en la canción)
+- Lista de reproducción
+- ️ Artwork de álbum
+- Reproducción en background
+- Controles de notificación
+
+## Testing
+
+El proyecto está preparado para:
+
+- Unit Tests (Domain Layer)
+- Integration Tests (Data Layer)
+- UI Tests (Presentation Layer)
+
+## Licencia
+
+Este proyecto es de código abierto y está disponible bajo la licencia MIT.
+
+## ‍ Autor
+
+Tu Nombre - [@tuusuario](https://github.com/tuusuario)
+
+## Contribuciones
+
+Las contribuciones son bienvenidas! Por favor:
+
+1. Fork el proyecto
+2. Crea una rama para tu feature (`git checkout -b feature/AmazingFeature`)
+3. Commit tus cambios (`git commit -m 'Add some AmazingFeature'`)
+4. Push a la rama (`git push origin feature/AmazingFeature`)
+5. Abre un Pull Request
+
+## Notas
+
+- Las canciones de ejemplo utilizan URLs de SoundHelix para demostración
+- Las imágenes de álbumes son de Spotify (solo para demostración)
+- En producción, deberías usar tu propia fuente de música y artwork
+
+## Próximas Características
+
+- [ ] Soporte para playlists personalizadas
+- [ ] Reproducción aleatoria y repetición
+- [ ] Búsqueda de canciones
+- [ ] Favoritos
+- [ ] Ecualizador
+- [ ] Lyrics/Letras
+- [ ] Integración con servicios de streaming
+
+---
+
+⭐ Si te gustó este proyecto, no olvides darle una estrella!
+

 val sessionToken = SessionToken(
 context,
 ComponentName(context, MusicService::class.java)
 )

 controllerFuture = MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync()
 controllerFuture?.addListener({
 mediaController = controllerFuture?.get()
 setupPlayerListener()
 }, MoreExecutors.directExecutor())
 }

 private fun setupPlayerListener() {
 mediaController?.addListener(object : Player.Listener {
 override fun onIsPlayingChanged(isPlaying: Boolean) {
 _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(isPlaying = isPlaying)
 }

 override fun onPlaybackStateChanged(playbackState: Int) {
 val state = when (playbackState) {
 Player.STATE_IDLE -> PlaybackState.IDLE
 Player.STATE_BUFFERING -> PlaybackState.BUFFERING
 Player.STATE_READY -> PlaybackState.READY
 Player.STATE_ENDED -> PlaybackState.ENDED
 else -> PlaybackState.IDLE
 }
 _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(
 playbackState = state,
 duration = mediaController?.duration ?: 0L
 )
 }

 override fun onMediaItemTransition(mediaItem: MediaItem?, reason: Int) {
 val currentIndex = mediaController?.currentMediaItemIndex ?: -1
 if (currentIndex >= 0 && currentIndex < currentPlaylist.size) {
 _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(
 currentSong = currentPlaylist[currentIndex]
 )
 }
 }
 })
 }

 override fun play() {
 mediaController?.play()
 }

 override fun pause() {
 mediaController?.pause()
 }

 override fun seekTo(position: Long) {
 mediaController?.seekTo(position)
 }

 override fun skipToNext() {
 mediaController?.seekToNext()
 }

 override fun skipToPrevious() {
 mediaController?.seekToPrevious()
 }

 override fun playSong(song: Song) {
 val mediaItem = createMediaItem(song)
 mediaController?.apply {
 setMediaItem(mediaItem)
 prepare()
 play()
 }
 _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(currentSong = song)
 }

 override fun setPlaylist(songs: List<Song>, startIndex: Int) {
 currentPlaylist = songs
 val mediaItems = songs.map { createMediaItem(it) }

 mediaController?.apply {
 setMediaItems(mediaItems, startIndex, 0)
 prepare()
 play()
 }

 if (startIndex < songs.size) {
 _playerState.value = _playerState.value.copy(currentSong = songs[startIndex])
 }
 }

 private fun createMediaItem(song: Song): MediaItem {
 val metadata = MediaMetadata.Builder()
 .setTitle(song.title)
 .setArtist(song.artist)
 .setAlbumTitle(song.album)
 .setArtworkUri(android.net.Uri.parse(song.imageUrl))
 .build()

 return MediaItem.Builder()
 .setMediaId(song.id)
 .setUri(song.mediaUri)
 .setMediaMetadata(metadata)
 .build()
 }

 override fun release() {
 MediaController.releaseFuture(controllerFuture ?: return)
 mediaController = null
 }
}

Lee música real del dispositivo y soporta reproducción en segundo plano.\n\n## Tabla de Contenidos\n\n- [Características](#características)\n- [Arquitectura](#arquitectura)\n- [Capas del Proyecto](#capas-del-proyecto)\n- [Componentes Principales](#componentes-principales)\n- [Tecnologías Utilizadas](#tecnologías-utilizadas)\n- [Permisos](#permisos)\n- [Instalación](#instalación)\n- [Flujo de Datos](#flujo-de-datos)\n- [Explicación Detallada del Código](#explicación-detallada-del-código)\n\n## ✨ Características\n\n- ✅ Lee música real del dispositivo usando **MediaStore**\n- ✅ Reproducción en segundo plano con **MediaSessionService**\n- ✅ Controles de reproducción: Play, Pause, Next, Previous\n- ✅ Barra de progreso con seek (arrastrar para cambiar posición)\n- ✅ Actualización en tiempo real de la posición de reproducción\n- ✅ UI moderna con **Jetpack Compose** y **Material Design 3**\n- ✅ Manejo de permisos en tiempo de ejecución\n- ✅ Artwork de álbum (carátulas)\n- ✅ Lista completa de canciones con desplazamiento\n\n## ️ Arquitectura\n\nEste proyecto implementa **Clean Architecture** dividiendo el código en 3 capas principales:\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ PRESENTATION LAYER │\n│ (UI, ViewModels, Compose Screens) │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n ↓ ↑\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ DOMAIN LAYER │\n│ (Use Cases, Entities, Repositories) │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n ↓ ↑\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ DATA LAYER │\n│ (Repositories Impl, Data Sources, │\n│ MediaSessionService) │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### Ventajas de Clean Architecture:\n\n1. **Testeable**: Cada capa puede probarse independientemente\n2. **Mantenible**: Código organizado y fácil de entender\n3. **Escalable**: Agregar nuevas features es sencillo\n4. **Desacoplado**: Las capas no dependen de implementaciones concretas\n5. **Independiente de frameworks**: La lógica de negocio no depende de Android\n\n## Capas del Proyecto\n\n### 1️⃣ Domain Layer (Capa de Dominio)\n\n**Ubicación**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/mediasessionplayer/domain/`\n\nEsta es la capa más interna y **no tiene dependencias** de Android. Contiene:\n\n#### **Modelos (Entities)**\n\n- **`Song.kt`**: Representa una canción\n ```kotlin\n data class Song(\n val id: String, // ID único\n val title: String, // Título de la canción\n val artist: String, // Artista\n val album: String, // Álbum\n val duration: Long, // Duración en milisegundos\n val imageUrl: String, // URI de la carátula\n val mediaUri: String // URI del archivo de audio\n )\n ```\n\n- **`PlayerState.kt`**: Estado del reproductor\n ```kotlin\n data class PlayerState(\n val currentSong: Song? = null, // Canción actual\n val isPlaying: Boolean = false, // ¿Está reproduciendo?\n val playbackState: PlaybackState, // Estado (IDLE, READY, etc.)\n val currentPosition: Long = 0L, // Posición actual en ms\n val duration: Long = 0L // Duración total en ms\n )\n ```\n\n#### **Interfaces de Repositorio**\n\nDefinen **qué operaciones** se pueden hacer, pero no **cómo** se hacen:\n\n- **`MusicRepository.kt`**: Obtener canciones del dispositivo\n- **`PlayerRepository.kt`**: Controlar la reproducción\n\n#### **Use Cases (Casos de Uso)**\n\nCada Use Case representa **una acción específica** del usuario:\n\n- **`GetSongsUseCase`**: Obtiene la lista de canciones\n- **`PlaySongUseCase`**: Reproduce una canción específica\n- **`GetPlayerStateUseCase`**: Observa el estado del reproductor\n- **`ControlPlaybackUseCase`**: Controla play, pause, seek, next, previous\n\n**¿Por qué Use Cases?** \n- Encapsulan la lógica de negocio\n- Son reutilizables\n- Facilitan el testing\n- Hacen el código más legible\n\n### 2️⃣ Data Layer (Capa de Datos)\n\n**Ubicación**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/mediasessionplayer/data/`\n\nImplementa las interfaces definidas en Domain y maneja datos reales:\n\n#### **Data Sources**\n\n- **`LocalMusicDataSource.kt`**: Lee música del dispositivo usando **MediaStore**\n - Consulta el `ContentResolver` de Android\n - Obtiene metadata: título, artista, álbum, duración\n - Construye URIs para reproducción y artwork\n\n#### **Repository Implementations**\n\n- **`MusicRepositoryImpl.kt`**: \n - Usa `LocalMusicDataSource` para obtener canciones\n - Cachea la lista para mejorar rendimiento\n \n- **`PlayerRepositoryImpl.kt`**: \n - Se conecta al `MediaController` (Media3)\n - Expone un `Flow<PlayerState>` reactivo\n - Actualiza la posición cada segundo mientras reproduce\n - Escucha cambios del player (play/pause, cambio de canción)\n\n#### **MediaSessionService**\n\n- **`MusicService.kt`**: \n - Hereda de `MediaSessionService`\n - Maneja reproducción en segundo plano\n - Crea notificación de media\n - Gestiona el ciclo de vida del player\n\n### 3️⃣ Presentation Layer (Capa de Presentación)\n\n**Ubicación**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/mediasessionplayer/presentation/`\n\nManeja la UI y la interacción con el usuario:\n\n#### **ViewModel**\n\n- **`MusicPlayerViewModel.kt`**:\n - Obtiene canciones usando Use Cases\n - Expone estados observables (Flow/StateFlow)\n - Maneja acciones del usuario (play, pause, seek)\n - Sobrevive a cambios de configuración\n\n#### **UI (Jetpack Compose)**\n\n- **`MusicPlayerScreen.kt`**:\n - **MusicPlayerScreen**: Pantalla principal con lista y mini player\n - **SongItem**: Item de lista con artwork, título, artista\n - **MiniPlayer**: Controles de reproducción en la parte inferior\n - **PlayerControls**: Botones de control (previous, play/pause, next)\n\n## ️ Componentes Principales\n\n### Media3 & MediaSession\n\n**Media3** es la nueva biblioteca de medios de Android (reemplazo de ExoPlayer):\n\n- **MediaController**: Cliente que controla el reproductor\n- **MediaSessionService**: Servicio que maneja reproducción en background\n- **MediaItem**: Representa un elemento multimedia\n- **Player.Listener**: Observa cambios en el reproductor\n\n### Dependency Injection (Hilt)\n\n**Hilt** es el framework de inyección de dependencias de Android:\n\n```kotlin\n@AndroidEntryPoint // En Activities, Fragments\n@HiltViewModel // En ViewModels\n@Inject // Para inyectar dependencias\n@Singleton // Para instancias únicas\n```\n\n**Módulo de Hilt** (`AppModule.kt`):\n- Provee instancias de repositorios\n- Vincula interfaces con implementaciones\n\n### Flows & State Management\n\n**Kotlin Flow** para manejar streams de datos reactivos:\n\n```kotlin\n// En el Repository\nprivate val _playerState = MutableStateFlow(PlayerState())\nval playerState: Flow<PlayerState> = _playerState.asStateFlow()\n\n// En el ViewModel\nval playerState: StateFlow<PlayerState> = getPlayerStateUseCase()\n .stateIn(scope = viewModelScope, ...)\n\n// En la UI\nval playerState by viewModel.playerState.collectAsState()\n```\n\n## Tecnologías Utilizadas\n\n- **Kotlin** 2.0.21\n- **Jetpack Compose** - +# Music Player - Media3 & MediaSession con Clean Architecture
+
+Un reproductor de música moderno para Android que utiliza **Media3**, **MediaSession** y **Clean
+Architecture**. Lee música real del dispositivo y soporta reproducción en segundo plano.
+
+## Tabla de Contenidos
+
+- [Características](#características)
+- [Arquitectura](#arquitectura)
+- [Capas del Proyecto](#capas-del-proyecto)

+- [Explicación Detallada del Código](#explicación-detallada-del-código)

+## ✨ Características
+
+- ✅ Lee música real del dispositivo usando **MediaStore**
+- ✅ Reproducción en segundo plano con **MediaSessionService**
+- ✅ Controles de reproducción: Play, Pause, Next, Previous
+- ✅ Barra de progreso con seek (arrastrar para cambiar posición)
+- ✅ Actualización en tiempo real de la posición de reproducción
+- ✅ UI moderna con **Jetpack Compose** y **Material Design 3**
+- ✅ Manejo de permisos en tiempo de ejecución
+- ✅ Artwork de álbum (carátulas)
+- ✅ Lista completa de canciones con desplazamiento
+
+## ️ Arquitectura
+
+Este proyecto implementa **Clean Architecture** dividiendo el código en 3 capas principales:
+
+```
+┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
+│ PRESENTATION LAYER │
+│ (UI, ViewModels, Compose Screens) │
+└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
+ ↓ ↑
+┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
+│ DOMAIN LAYER │
+│ (Use Cases, Entities, Repositories) │
+└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
+ ↓ ↑
+┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
+│ DATA LAYER │
+│ (Repositories Impl, Data Sources, │
+│ MediaSessionService) │
+└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+### Ventajas de Clean Architecture:
+
+1. **Testeable**: Cada capa puede probarse independientemente
+2. **Mantenible**: Código organizado y fácil de entender
+3. **Escalable**: Agregar nuevas features es sencillo
+4. **Desacoplado**: Las capas no dependen de implementaciones concretas
+5. **Independiente de frameworks**: La lógica de negocio no depende de Android
+
+## Capas del Proyecto
+
+### 1️⃣ Domain Layer (Capa de Dominio)
+
+**Ubicación**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/mediasessionplayer/domain/`
+
+Esta es la capa más interna y **no tiene dependencias** de Android. Contiene:
+
+#### **Modelos (Entities)**
+
+- **`Song.kt`**: Representa una canción
+ ```kotlin
+ data class Song(
+ val id: String, // ID único
+ val title: String, // Título de la canción
+ val artist: String, // Artista
+ val album: String, // Álbum
+ val duration: Long, // Duración en milisegundos
+ val imageUrl: String, // URI de la carátula
+ val mediaUri: String // URI del archivo de audio
+ )
+ ```
+
+- **`PlayerState.kt`**: Estado del reproductor
+ ```kotlin
+ data class PlayerState(
+ val currentSong: Song? = null, // Canción actual
+ val isPlaying: Boolean = false, // ¿Está reproduciendo?
+ val playbackState: PlaybackState, // Estado (IDLE, READY, etc.)
+ val currentPosition: Long = 0L, // Posición actual en ms
+ val duration: Long = 0L // Duración total en ms
+ )
+ ```
+
+#### **Interfaces de Repositorio**
+
+Definen **qué operaciones** se pueden hacer, pero no **cómo** se hacen:
+
+- **`MusicRepository.kt`**: Obtener canciones del dispositivo
+- **`PlayerRepository.kt`**: Controlar la reproducción
+
+#### **Use Cases (Casos de Uso)**
+
+Cada Use Case representa **una acción específica** del usuario:
+
+- **`GetSongsUseCase`**: Obtiene la lista de canciones
+- **`PlaySongUseCase`**: Reproduce una canción específica
+- **`GetPlayerStateUseCase`**: Observa el estado del reproductor
+- **`ControlPlaybackUseCase`**: Controla play, pause, seek, next, previous
+
+**¿Por qué Use Cases?**
+
+- Encapsulan la lógica de negocio
+- Son reutilizables
+- Facilitan el testing
+- Hacen el código más legible
+
+### 2️⃣ Data Layer (Capa de Datos)
+
+**Ubicación**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/mediasessionplayer/data/`
+
+Implementa las interfaces definidas en Domain y maneja datos reales:
+
+#### **Data Sources**
+
+- **`LocalMusicDataSource.kt`**: Lee música del dispositivo usando **MediaStore**
+ - Consulta el `ContentResolver` de Android
+ - Obtiene metadata: título, artista, álbum, duración
+ - Construye URIs para reproducción y artwork
+
+#### **Repository Implementations**
+
+- **`MusicRepositoryImpl.kt`**:
+ - Usa `LocalMusicDataSource` para obtener canciones
+ - Cachea la lista para mejorar rendimiento
+
+- **`PlayerRepositoryImpl.kt`**:
+ - Se conecta al `MediaController` (Media3)
+ - Expone un `Flow<PlayerState>` reactivo
+ - Actualiza la posición cada segundo mientras reproduce
+ - Escucha cambios del player (play/pause, cambio de canción)
+
+#### **MediaSessionService**
+
+- **`MusicService.kt`**:
+ - Hereda de `MediaSessionService`
+ - Maneja reproducción en segundo plano
+ - Crea notificación de media
+ - Gestiona el ciclo de vida del player
+
+### 3️⃣ Presentation Layer (Capa de Presentación)
+
+**Ubicación**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/mediasessionplayer/presentation/`
+
+Maneja la UI y la interacción con el usuario:
+
+#### **ViewModel**
+
+- **`MusicPlayerViewModel.kt`**:
+ - Obtiene canciones usando Use Cases
+ - Expone estados observables (Flow/StateFlow)
+ - Maneja acciones del usuario (play, pause, seek)
+ - Sobrevive a cambios de configuración
+
+#### **UI (Jetpack Compose)**
+
+- **`MusicPlayerScreen.kt`**:
+ - **MusicPlayerScreen**: Pantalla principal con lista y mini player
+ - **SongItem**: Item de lista con artwork, título, artista
+ - **MiniPlayer**: Controles de reproducción en la parte inferior
+ - **PlayerControls**: Botones de control (previous, play/pause, next)

+- Vincula interfaces con implementaciones

+- La coroutine se ejecuta cada segundo
+- Obtiene la posición actual del MediaController
+- Actualiza el StateFlow
+- La UI (Compose) observa el StateFlow y se recompone automáticamente
+
+### 4. Creación de MediaItem
+
+```kotlin
+private fun createMediaItem(song: Song): MediaItem {
+ val metadata = MediaMetadata.Builder()
+ .setTitle(song.title)
+ .setArtist(song.artist)
+ .setAlbumTitle(song.album)
+ .setArtworkUri(Uri.parse(song.imageUrl))
+ .build()
+
+ return MediaItem.Builder()
+ .setMediaId(song.id)
+ .setUri(song.mediaUri) // URI del audio
+ .setMediaMetadata(metadata) // Metadata para notificación
+ .build()
+}
+```
+
+**MediaMetadata** se usa para:
+
+- Mostrar información en la notificación
+- Controles de media en pantalla de bloqueo
+- Integración con Android Auto
+
+### 5. MusicService (MediaSessionService)
+
+```kotlin
+@AndroidEntryPoint
+class MusicService : MediaSessionService() {
+ 
+ override fun onCreate() {
+ super.onCreate()
+ 
+ // Crear ExoPlayer
+ val player = ExoPlayer.Builder(this).build()
+ 
+ // Crear MediaSession
+ mediaSession = MediaSession.Builder(this, player).build()
+ }
+ 
+ override fun onGetSession(controllerInfo: MediaSession.ControllerInfo): MediaSession? {
+ return mediaSession
+ }
+}
+```
+
+**¿Por qué MediaSessionService?**
+
+- Permite reproducción en background
+- Crea notificación automáticamente
+- Integra con controles del sistema (Bluetooth, audífonos)
+- Gestiona focus de audio
+
+### 6. ViewModel y UI
+
+**ViewModel** orquesta los Use Cases:
+
+```kotlin
+fun playSong(song: Song) {
+ val currentSongs = _songs.value
+ val index = currentSongs.indexOf(song)
+ if (index != -1) {
+ // Establece toda la playlist
+ controlPlaybackUseCase.setPlaylist(currentSongs, index)
+ }
+}
+```
+
+**UI** observa estados y reacciona:
+
+```kotlin
+val playerState by viewModel.playerState.collectAsState()
+
+// Cuando playerState cambia, Compose recompone
+MiniPlayer(
+ currentSong = playerState.currentSong,
+ isPlaying = playerState.isPlaying,
+ currentPosition = playerState.currentPosition,
+ duration = playerState.duration,
+ onPlayPauseClick = { viewModel.playPause() },
+ onSeek = { viewModel.seekTo(it) }
+)
+```
+
+## Patrones y Principios Aplicados
+
+### SOLID Principles
+
+1. **Single Responsibility**: Cada clase tiene una única responsabilidad
+ - `LocalMusicDataSource` → Solo lee música del dispositivo
+ - `PlayerRepositoryImpl` → Solo maneja reproducción
+
+2. **Open/Closed**: Abierto a extensión, cerrado a modificación
+ - Interfaces permiten diferentes implementaciones sin cambiar código
+
+3. **Liskov Substitution**: Las implementaciones pueden reemplazar interfaces
+ - `MusicRepositoryImpl` puede reemplazarse por otra implementación
+
+4. **Interface Segregation**: Interfaces específicas y pequeñas
+ - `MusicRepository` y `PlayerRepository` separados
+
+5. **Dependency Inversion**: Depender de abstracciones
+ - ViewModel depende de Use Cases (abstracciones), no de implementaciones
+
+### Otros Patrones
+
+- **Repository Pattern**: Abstrae el origen de los datos
+- **Observer Pattern**: Flows para observar cambios
+- **Dependency Injection**: Hilt para gestionar dependencias
+- **MVVM**: ViewModel + UI reactiva
+
+## Testing
+
+La arquitectura facilita testing:
+
+```kotlin
+// Test de Use Case (sin Android)
+class GetSongsUseCaseTest {
+ @Test
+ fun `test get songs returns list`() = runTest {
+ val mockRepo = mockk<MusicRepository>()
+ coEvery { mockRepo.getSongs() } returns listOf(mockSong)
+ 
+ val useCase = GetSongsUseCase(mockRepo)
+ val result = useCase()
+ 
+ assertEquals(1, result.size)
+ }
+}
+```
+

+## Componentes y sus Responsabilidades
+
+### Domain Layer
+
+#### **Song (Entity)**
+
+```kotlin
+// Representa una canción en el dominio
+// No tiene lógica, solo datos
+data class Song(
+ val id: String,
+ val title: String,
+ val artist: String,
+ val album: String,
+ val duration: Long,
+ val imageUrl: String,
+ val mediaUri: String
+)
+```
+
+**Responsabilidad**: Ser una representación pura de datos sin dependencias de Android.
+
+#### **MusicRepository (Interface)**
+
+```kotlin
+// Define QUÉ se puede hacer, no CÓMO
+interface MusicRepository {
+ suspend fun getSongs(): List<Song>
+ fun getSongById(id: String): Song?
+}
+```
+
+**Responsabilidad**: Contrato para obtener música, sin saber de dónde viene.
+
+#### **Use Cases**
+
+```kotlin
+// Encapsula una acción específica del usuario
+class GetSongsUseCase @Inject constructor(
+ private val repository: MusicRepository
+) {
+ suspend operator fun invoke(): List<Song> = repository.getSongs()
+}
+```
+
+**Responsabilidad**:
+
+- Una única acción
+- Lógica de negocio si la hay
+- Coordinación entre repositorios si es necesario
+

+
+#### **LocalMusicDataSource**
+
+```kotlin
+@Singleton
+class LocalMusicDataSource @Inject constructor(
+ @ApplicationContext private val context: Context
+) {
+ fun getLocalSongs(): List<Song> {
+ // Query MediaStore
+ // Parse Cursor
+ // Build Song objects
+ }
+}
+```
+
+**Responsabilidad**: Acceso directo al sistema de archivos de Android.
+
+#### **PlayerRepositoryImpl**
+

+## Decisiones de Diseño
+
+### ¿Por qué Use Cases en lugar de llamar directamente al Repository?
+
+✅ **Con Use Cases:**
+
+```kotlin
+// ViewModel
+fun playSong(song: Song) {
+ playSongUseCase(song)
+}
+
+// Use Case - puede tener lógica compleja
+class PlaySongUseCase {
+ operator fun invoke(song: Song) {
+ // Validar canción
+ // Registrar en analytics
+ // Actualizar historial
+ // Reproducir
+ }
+}
+```
+
+❌ **Sin Use Cases:**
+
+```kotlin
+// ViewModel - demasiada lógica aquí
+fun playSong(song: Song) {
+ // Validar canción
+ // Registrar en analytics
+ // Actualizar historial
+ playerRepository.playSong(song)
+}
+```
+
+### ¿Por qué separar MusicRepository y PlayerRepository?
+
+**Separation of Concerns:**
+
+- `MusicRepository`: Obtener datos (READ)
+- `PlayerRepository`: Control de reproducción (CONTROL)
+
+Permite cambiar la fuente de música sin afectar el reproductor.
+
+### ¿Por qué usar Flow en lugar de LiveData?
+
+✅ **Flow:**
+
+- Parte de Kotlin (no Android)
+- Más operadores
+- Mejor con Coroutines
+- Type-safe
+- Composable
+
+### ¿Por qué MediaSessionService en lugar de Service normal?
+
+✅ **MediaSessionService:**
+
+- Notificación automática
+- Integración con sistema
+- Controles en pantalla de bloqueo
+- Android Auto / Wear OS
+- Gestión de audio focus
+

+## Principios SOLID Aplicados
+
+### S - Single Responsibility Principle
+
+- `LocalMusicDataSource`: Solo lee del MediaStore
+- `PlayerRepositoryImpl`: Solo maneja reproducción
+- `MusicService`: Solo maneja servicio de background
+
+### O - Open/Closed Principle
+
+- Interfaces permiten extender funcionalidad sin modificar código existente
+- Podemos agregar `RemoteMusicDataSource` sin cambiar `MusicRepository`
+
+### L - Liskov Substitution Principle
+
+- `MusicRepositoryImpl` puede sustituirse por cualquier implementación
+- `PlayerRepositoryImpl` puede ser mock para testing
+
+### I - Interface Segregation Principle
+
+- Interfaces pequeñas y específicas
+- `MusicRepository` ≠ `PlayerRepository`
+
+### D - Dependency Inversion Principle
+
+- ViewModel depende de abstracciones (Use Cases)
+- Use Cases dependen de interfaces (Repositories)
+- Nadie depende de implementaciones concretas
+
+## Ventajas para Testing
+
+```kotlin
+// Unit Test - ViewModel (sin Android)
+@Test
+fun `play song updates state`() = runTest {
+ // Mock repositories
+ val mockPlayerRepo = mockk<PlayerRepository>()
+ val mockMusicRepo = mockk<MusicRepository>()
+ 
+ // Create use cases with mocks
+ val playSongUseCase = PlaySongUseCase(mockPlayerRepo)
+ 
+ // Create ViewModel
+ val viewModel = MusicPlayerViewModel(...)
+ 
+ // Test
+ viewModel.playSong(testSong)
+ 
+ // Verify
+ verify { mockPlayerRepo.playSong(testSong) }
+}
+```
+
+## Escalabilidad
+
+### Agregar nueva fuente de música:
+
+```kotlin
+// 1. Crear nuevo DataSource
+class SpotifyMusicDataSource @Inject constructor(
+ private val spotifyApi: SpotifyApi
+) {
+ suspend fun getSpotifySongs(): List<Song> { }
+}
+
+// 2. Actualizar Repository
+class MusicRepositoryImpl @Inject constructor(
+ private val localDataSource: LocalMusicDataSource,
+ private val spotifyDataSource: SpotifyMusicDataSource
+) : MusicRepository {
+ override suspend fun getSongs(): List<Song> {
+ return localDataSource.getLocalSongs() + 
+ spotifyDataSource.getSpotifySongs()
+ }
+}
+
+// 3. ¡Nada más! Use Cases y UI no cambian
+```
+
+### Agregar nueva feature (Favoritos):
+
+```kotlin
+// 1. Agregar al modelo
+data class Song(
+ // ... existing fields
+ val isFavorite: Boolean = false
+)
+
+// 2. Crear Use Case
+class ToggleFavoriteUseCase @Inject constructor(
+ private val repository: MusicRepository
+) {
+ suspend operator fun invoke(songId: String) { }
+}
+
+// 3. Actualizar ViewModel
+fun toggleFavorite(songId: String) {
+ viewModelScope.launch {
+ toggleFavoriteUseCase(songId)
+ }
+}
+
+// 4. Actualizar UI
+IconButton(onClick = { viewModel.toggleFavorite(song.id) }) {
+ Icon(Icons.Default.Favorite)
+}
+```
